alias: Purifier — run after the cat toilet
description: v4. Runs the corridor purifier after a cat visit for up to ~28 minutes, ending early ONLY if the PM2.5 sensor proved it is responsive (rose after the visit) and then came back down. A sensor pinned at its floor gets no vote and the full window runs. The start is confirmed by WAITING for the fan to report on, never by reading its state at a guessed offset: this device reports on optimistically, then flips back to off when the integration polls it, and only settles on for real about 18 seconds later. Shutdown depends on a run-local fact, and if the start cannot be confirmed the fan is commanded off rather than abandoned.

actions.note:
v4, after the SECOND live incident. Measured from history, 2026-09-20 22:23:

  22:23:05.19  fan -> on     our fan.turn_on, reported optimistically
  22:23:06.38  fan -> off    the miio integration polled the device, which had not acted yet
  22:23:10     (our read)    saw 'off' -> declared FAILED TO START, released, stopped
  22:23:23.14  fan -> on     the device actually started, motor 1524

The run abandoned ownership while the fan was coming on, so nothing owned it and nothing would stop it. It ran 46 minutes until the operator noticed. Worse, already_running (fan on, flag off) would have made EVERY future visit abort, silently, for ever.

This is the climate unit_moved bug again, in a new device: READING A DEVICE'S STATE TOO SOON AFTER COMMANDING IT AND MISTAKING THE RESULT FOR FAILURE. I wrote 'never assume the service call worked' in v2 and then implemented the check as a single sample at a guessed 5-second offset, which is the same error with the opposite sign.

THE FIX IS TO STOP SAMPLING AT A GUESS. The start is now confirmed by WAITING for the fan to report on and hold it for 15 seconds, with a 120-second timeout. That is self-timing: it costs nothing when the device is quick, it ignores the 1.2-second optimistic blip because of the 'for', and it tolerates a device that takes 18 seconds - or 60 - without any constant needing to be right. The same 'for: 15 seconds' is now on the human-stop trigger, so the identical optimistic-then-corrected flap cannot be misread as a person switching the fan off mid-run.

IF THE START IS NEVER CONFIRMED, THE FAN IS COMMANDED OFF. Abandoning was what stranded it. Leaving the world as we found it is the only safe exit.

ALREADY_RUNNING NOW SPEAKS. It is still right to refuse a fan somebody else started, but a silent refusal is how a stranded fan would have disabled this automation permanently without a word. It now writes a line to input_text.purifier_last_run saying why it did nothing.

STILL TRUE from earlier versions: the visit guard rejects the midnight reset, a restart restore and a repeated report; recovery fires on reload as well as restart; a manual stop suppresses re-starts for 30 minutes; the early stop is armed only if PM2.5 actually rose.
